Uncloud vs. Nextcloud: a private cloud without the server admin.

Both keep your files off somebody else’s servers. Uncloud is built for a household.

Nextcloud is a full self-hosted suite. Uncloud is one app that turns a computer at home into your family’s cloud in minutes.

Coming from Nextcloud

Move a household over in three steps.

Your Nextcloud files are already on a drive you control. Uncloud copies them into each person’s own space.

  1. 1

    Install Uncloud at home

    Open the Mac app and choose Make this Mac the Uncloud host. Make your account and pick where everyone’s files live.

  2. 2

    Add your Nextcloud folder

    Click Add files, choose This computer, and add the folder the Nextcloud desktop client keeps, or the drive your files are on.

  3. 3

    Add everyone else

    Open People and click Add someone. Each person gets their own username, password and private space.

Questions

Uncloud vs. Nextcloud questions

Is Uncloud built on Nextcloud?

+

No. Uncloud is its own app. It uses Syncthing to keep laptops in sync and Tailscale, a free service, for its secure connection from anywhere.

Which is easier to set up?

+

On a Mac, Uncloud sets up in five minutes or less: open the app, choose Make this Mac the Uncloud host, make your account and pick a folder. Nextcloud is usually installed on a server with Docker, or with a web server, PHP and a database.

Do I need a domain name or open ports?

+

Not with Uncloud. Turn on remote access and Uncloud gives you a secure https:// address that works at home and away, on any device.

When is Nextcloud the better fit?

+

If you want calendars, contacts, office documents, chat and a large app ecosystem on one server, Nextcloud covers far more ground. Uncloud focuses on your household’s files.

What does Uncloud cost?

+

Uncloud Home is $99 once. Join early access to lock in $79 at launch, with a 30-day free trial and no credit card. Unlimited household members and devices, remote access, migrations and software updates are included.
